RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the December 2, 2003 /Agrahayana 11, 1925 (Saka)
————
(Ministries:  Civil Aviation; Finance; Petroleum and Natural Gas; Tourism
and Culture; Water Resources)
Total number of questions—20
1
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Provision for CNG  in cities
†*1. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the
Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the cities in the country where
C.N.G. is proposed to be provided for the
plying of buses during the next year;
(b) whether the Ministry is considering
to open a C.N.G. filling station in Dehradun,
the capital of Uttaranchal; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Status of tourism industry
*2. SHRI K. RAHMAN KHAN: Will
the Minister of TOURISM AND
CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the present status of tourism
industry of the country as compared to
those of prominent countries; and
(b) what is the expectation for the
current year and the steps taken to reach
the target of three million international
tourists for the country?
Profits of overseas branches of SBI
and IOB
*3. SHRI AMAR SINGH: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there had
been drastic fall in the net profit of overseas
branches of State Bank of India and Indian
Overseas Bank during 2001-2002; if so, the
details thereof and the reasons therefor;
(b) what is the position of these banks
reflected during the year 2002-2003; and
(c) what steps have been taken to
improve the situation?
Pipeline for transportation of oil
†*4. SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
SHRI LAJPAT RAI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a project for
laying of pipelines for transportation of oil
has been prepared by certain public sector
oil companies and sent for Government's
approval;
(b) if so, the names of the companies by
which such proposals have been sent to
Government by October, 2003; and

2
(c) the rate at which the dividend is
expected to accrue on the capital invested
in these projects?
Foreign investment in several
sectors
*5. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
propose to allow increased foreign
investment in insurance, telecom, aviation,
coffee and rubber plantations;
(b) whether it is also a fact that easier
norms have been drawn for foreign
investment in banks, small industries and
petroleum retailing; and
(c) if so, the details of Government policy
in this regard for the above sectors?
Linking of Mahanadi and Vaigal rivers
*6. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO:
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to take
up linking of Mahanadi with Vaigal rivers
early to tackle the problem of recurrent
floods and droughts in different parts of the
country;
(b) if so, by when the link-work would
start; and
(c) if not, in what manner water
requirements in Andhra Pradesh which are
to be taken up with a national perspective,
are proposed to be solved?
Fake currency notes
*7. DR. ABRAR AHMED:
DR. DASARI NARAYANA
RAO:
Will the Minister  of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have made
any assessment about the fake Indian
currency notes in circulation as on date;
(b) whether Government have reasons
to believe that Pakistan Government is
behind this fake Indian currency notes
circulation; and
(c) if so, the steps Government have
taken in this regard?
Trade to Trade deals in BSE
*8. SHRI SANJAY NIRUPAM: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether SEBI has banned Trade to
Trade deals in Bombay Stock Exchange;
and
(b) if so, the details of the companies
which have been banned and the reasons
therefor?
Fraud cases in banks
*9. DR. DASARI NARAYANA RAO:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether quite a good number of fraud
cases have come to light in banking sector
in which banks were defrauded substantial
amount of money;
(b) if so, the details of frauds detected in
each bank during the last three years,
year-wise and bank-wise;
(c) in how many cases, insiders were
involved, bank-wise; and
(d) the action taken by each bank,
year-wise?

3
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Interest rate on deposits
†*10. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH
'LALAN':
SHRI LAJPAT RAI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that rate of interest
on deposits was reduced from time to time
by Public Sector Banks during the period
from March, 2000 to October, 2003;
(b) if so, the extent of reduction in the
rate of interest made by each of the Public
Sector Banks alongwith the dates on which
such reduction was made; and
(c) the rates of interest that were in force
for the various term deposits schemes in
these banks at the end of  April, 2000 and
October, 2003?
Right to contamination-free water to
domestic users
*11. SHRI MANOJ
BHATTACHARYA:
SHRI P. PRABHAKAR
REDDY:
Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Delhi Jal
Board Act, 1996 does not recognise the right
of the consumer to be supplied with
contamination-free water to the domestic
users;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and
whether Government propose to correct this
inadequacy in law to give a legal cover
against unsafe water supply; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Pagladiya Dam in Assam
*12. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Assam
Chief Minister has urged upon the Central
Government to constitute an autonomous
body for ensuring the timely completion
of the multi-purpose Pagladiya Dam project
in the State;
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
and
(c) by when the proposed autonomous
body is likely to be put in place?
Revision of rates of interest on loans
†*13. SHRI LAJPAT RAI:
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the rate of
interest on the loan given to different
sectors from time to time during April, 2000
to October, 2003 by Public Sector Banks
in the country has been revised;
(b) if so, when these changes have been
made together with the details thereof; and
(c) the rates of interest being charged on
different kinds of loans given to various
sectors by Public Sector Banks during April,
2000 and October, 2003?
Financial performance of IA
*14.SHRI MOOLCHAND MEENA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Indian Airlines has been
continuously incurring loss which has been
commented by the CAG in its latest report;
(b) whether delay in aircraft fleet
maintenance, poor revenue management,
injudicious implementation of the
promotional fares and underutilisation of
cargo capacity were the main reasons given
by the CAG;

4
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) whether IA is expected to post a net
loss of Rs. 93.98 crores in the first six
months (April-September) of the current
fiscal year; and
(d) if so, steps Government propose to
take to improve its position after CAG's
report?
Fake stamp papers
†*15. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some fake
stamp papers have been seized in some
banks during the recent past;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of persons found involved
in the same?
Excavations at Qutab Heritage
*16. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ:
Will the Minister of TOURISM AND
CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that out of many
artefacts found during excavations at Qutab
Heritage Complex, only 18 were last shifted
out in 1998 and the rest are left unattended
although many of these artefacts are from
the 27-odd Jain and Hindu temples that were
discovered in the Complex during ASI
operations;
(b) if so, the reasons for this gross neglect
which might have resulted in theft and
pilferage of such important historical pieces;
and
(c) what steps are proposed to be taken
to safeguard and interpret these artefacts
to enrich his torical records?
Low credit offtake by industry
*17. SHRI GAYA SINGH:
SHRI V.V. RAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite the
low interest rate regime, the credit offtake
from banks by industry continues to be
sluggish; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor?
Inquiry report on helicopter
accident
*18. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
SHRI AMAR SINGH:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Inquiry Commission on
the helicopter accident set up by
Government in August, 2003 to enquire
into safety and security of lives in offshore
operation especially air logistics and
inspection, mechanism, has since submitted
its report;
(b) if so, the salient features of the
recommendations made by it; and
(c) what is Government's reaction
thereto?
Retrieval of articles belonging to Sikh
Gurus
*19. SHRI RUMANDLA RAAMA-
CHANDRAYYA: Will the Minister of
TOURISM AND CULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that articles
belonging to Guru Nanak Dev and Guru
Gobind Singh have been allegedly shifted
to Canada; and

5
(b) if so, the measures proposed to bring
them back from Canada for preservation in
the country?
Lack of activity in primary issues
*20. SHRI NILOTPAL BASU: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the bullish
upward movement in the secondary market
in the stock exchanges during the last six
months in the secondary sector is not
commensurate with the number of primary
issues;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether the relative lack of activity
in primary issues which indicates domestic
investment can be construed as reason for
a 'feel good factor' of the economy?
